title: Coherent adic conditions for direct image with closed ambient support
statement: Let $j:Y\to X$ be an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] of Noetherian schemes [pqf-def-locnoeth], $K$ a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf on $X$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal], and $F:\mathbb N^{op}\to\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal O_Y)$ an inverse system [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Suppose $F$ satisfies the coherent formal object conditions for $K\mathcal O_Y$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Let $T\subseteq X$ be closed and contained in $j(Y)$, and suppose the nonzero-stalk support of every $F_n$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base] is contained in $j^{-1}(T)$. Then the actual inverse system $(j_*F_n)$, with the direct images of the given transition maps [def-pc-module-pullback], satisfies the coherent formal object conditions for $K$. No formal-system existence or algebraization conclusion is asserted.

source.place: Theorem Tag 088E, theorem-grothendieck-existence, proof: paragraph after Chow’s lemma, through formation of the extended coherent formal system; Lemma Tag 0CYJ, lemma-pushforward-coherent-on-open

proof.text: Identify Y with the open range U of j via j.isoOpensRange, and transport each module and transition through this isomorphism. The closed subset T lies in U. Apply coherent pushforward on an open to each coherent F_n; its direct image is coherent on X and zero on X minus T. Direct-image composition identifies this with the actual j_*F_n.

On U the natural restriction/direct-image counit identifies the direct-image system with F, and identifies the restricted ideal with K.comap j. Restriction preserves cokernels and ideal-power multiplication images, so the given annihilation and quotient-transition identities hold there. On X minus T the system is zero, hence so are its ideal-power products and quotient objects.

U and X minus T cover X. The multiplication images are zero on both opens and therefore globally. By multiplication naturality, each transition kills the indicated ideal-power multiplication image since its target is annihilated. Factor it through the cokernel projection. The factor is an isomorphism on U by the given quotient-transition condition and on X minus T between zero objects. It is an isomorphism globally by the sheaf-module open-cover isomorphism criterion. The factor equations with the quotient projections hold by the cokernel construction. Together with coherence these give precisely IsCoherentFormalModule K of the direct-image system.
